entries.title: Automated code review of the command line tool
Supply chain: relay and website
entries.result: No malicious or hijacked package among 308; every registry signature verified. 1 high, 1 medium in deploy and build setup.

entries.title: Supply chain: command line tool
entries.result: No malicious, hijacked or typosquatted crate among 405; all from crates.io. 1 high (release build setup, fixed), 9 medium, 10 low.

entries.title: Supply chain: iPhone and Android apps
entries.result: No malicious, hijacked or typosquatted package among 318 crates and the Android libraries; no remote Swift packages. 3 medium and 6 low in build controls; 1 low: a known SQLite advisory in a bundled library.

entries.title: Staging incident: retries after the relay refused a call
entries.result: 1 medium. Fixed in the command line tool and the relay; the app fix is in review.

continuous: From 23 November 2026, every change to the main branch of a public repository goes through a pull request and an independent review before merging (internal, AI-assisted).
The command line tool's parsers are fuzzed on every pull request that changes them, and nightly.

Dependencies: the command line tool's crates are checked on each pull request for known advisories, licences and sources (cargo deny) and against reviewed audits (cargo vet); the relay's and website's npm packages install only from the lockfile with registry signatures verified in CI; Dependabot reports advisories everywhere; routine updates wait 7 days after release (security updates don't wait).
Secret scanning with push protection on every public repository.
Shared protocol test vectors, checked byte for byte by the core, the relay and both apps.
Power-cut tests: unsealing is cut at every step and must resume without losing anything.
